MiniMax M3.1 Flash: Space Performance + Bunny Speed

🚀🐰 Yes, Space Bunny  - which has topped global leaderboards with 200T+ tokens - was an earlier version of M3.1 Flash.

💰Redefining the performance economics of agentic AI. M3.1 Flash achieves frontier-level intelligence across key tasks such as Cowork (Automation-Bench: 62%; ALE: 30%), Coding (DeepSWE: 74%) and Visual Reasoning (BabyVision: 91%), at 1/3 the cost of M3 and 3x the speed.

API pricing (flat rate): $0.15 / $0.60 per 1M input/output tokens, with cache reads at $0.015 / 1M tokens.

Model weights will arrive on Oct 23.

MiniMax M3.1 Flash, on more of your hardware.

Quantizing a 428B model opens up more ways to run it locally. Lower-bit weights reduce the memory needed to load the model and the weight data moved during decoding. Making those savings useful takes careful calibration, efficient low-bit kernels, and hardware-aware placement of experts across GPU and system RAM.

Thank you to the builders doing that work:

• @UnslothAI @danielhanchen — 2-bit Dynamic GGUF weights at 143.9 GB, with calibration and fidelity testing across coding, tool use and other workloads.
• @ViC305 — SAGE-EXL3, token-level fidelity measurements and a single-DGX-Spark recipe.
• @PeasantSmith — Project Maya quants and expert offloading for local coding and tool use.
• @MiaAI_lab — EXL3-EAQ quantization work.
• @jundotkim + mlx-community — oQ quants and DSpark-powered decoding through oMLX on Apple Silicon.
• @AIatAMD — Quark MXFP4 adapted for AMD Instinct.
• @atomic_chat_hq — GGUFs for local desktop workflows.
• @superalesha — custom inference work combining quantized weights, expert caching and system RAM on 4× RTX 3090.
Every shared quant, kernel, measurement and recipe gives the next builder a better starting point. Thank you.

MiniMax M3.1 Flash meets the @UnslothAI community. 🐙🦥✨

Unsloth’s Dynamic GGUFs bring our 428B MoE model to a 143.9GB 2-bit footprint, with 91.5% top-1 token agreement in their evaluation across seven domains.

That means a lower memory barrier to self-hosting, deployment through Unsloth Desktop and llama.cpp, and an OpenAI-compatible API for existing apps and agents.

With 78K+ GitHub stars and over 500M model downloads on Hugging Face, Unsloth gives M3.1 Flash a path into an established community of developers running, evaluating and building with open models.

Open weights. Local control. More ways to build.
Thank you 0G and the community for your support of M3.1 Flash! Hope to see more exciting projects from the community!

More reference control. Fewer denoising steps. More places to run H3.

The latest community contributions span 8-step reference-conditioned video + audio, 4-step distillation, sparse attention, and reference-token compression - alongside serving and workflow integrations across GPU servers, TPUs, and Apple Silicon.

What matters is what this enables: more affordable experimentation, finer creative control, and more choices about where and how video generation runs. Open models become more useful when the community can improve the methods, adapt the runtime, and build workflows around them.
